subject: integrated-science
general_outcomes: By the end of Junior School, the learner should be able to:
acquire scientific knowledge, skills, values and attitudes to make informed choices on career pathways at Senior School.
select, improvise, and safely use basic scientific tools, apparatus, materials and chemicals effectively in everyday life.
explore, manipulate, manage, and conserve the environment for learning and sustainable development.
practise relevant hygiene, sanitation, and nutrition skills to promote good health.
apply the understanding of body systems with a view to promote and maintain good health.
develop capacity for scientific inquiry and problem-solving in different situations.
appreciate the use of scientific knowledge, skills, principles, and practises in everyday life.
apply acquired scientific knowledge, skills, principles, and practises in everyday life.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to identify common hazards and their symbols in the laboratory.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: The learner identifies common hazards and their symbols in the laboratory exhaustively.
assessment_rubric.meets: The learner identifies common hazards and their symbols in the laboratory satisfactorily.
assessment_rubric.approaches: The learner identifies most of the common hazards and their symbols in the laboratory correctly.
assessment_rubric.below: The learner identifies a few common hazards and their symbols in the laboratory correctly

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to describe First Aid measures for common laboratory accidents.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: The learner describes all First Aid measures for common laboratory accidents systematically and comprehensibly.
assessment_rubric.meets: The learner describes all First Aid measures for common laboratory accidents systematically.
assessment_rubric.approaches: The learner describes most First Aid measures for common laboratory accidents systematically.
assessment_rubric.below: The learner describes a few First Aid measures for common laboratory accidents systematically.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: The learner uses and cares for all apparatus and instruments in the laboratory innovatively.
assessment_rubric.meets: The learner uses and cares for all apparatus and instruments in the laboratory.
assessment_rubric.approaches: The learner uses and cares for most of the apparatus and instruments in the laboratory.
assessment_rubric.below: The learner uses but care cares for a few apparatus or instruments in the laboratory.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to use the SI units for basic and derived quantities.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: The learner uses all the SI units for basic and derived quantities correctly giving examples.
assessment_rubric.meets: The learner uses all the SI units for basic and derived quantities correctly.
assessment_rubric.approaches: The learner uses most of the SI units for basic and derived quantities correctly.
assessment_rubric.below: The learner uses a few of the SI units for basic and derived quantities.

substrands.name: Introduction to Integrated Science
learning_outcomes: outline the components of Integrated Science as a field of study
explain the importance of science in daily life
show interest in learning Integrated Science at junior school.
learning_experiences: brainstorm on the components of Integrated Science
use digital or print media to search for information on components of integrated science and share with peers
collaboratively discuss the importance of science in daily life
search for information from print or digital media on pathways related to Integrated Science at Senior School, Project
use locally available materials to construct a career chart and display.
inquiry_questions: How is the knowledge acquired in Integrated Science useful in daily life?
core_competencies: Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and Collaboration: the learner acquires listening and speaking skills as they discuss the importance of science in daily life.
Digital Literacy: the learner acquires digital manipulative skills as they search for information from digital media on pathways related to Integrated Science at Senior School. Values:
Respect: the learner respects each other’s opinion(s) as they discuss the importance of scientific knowledge in daily life.

Unity: the learner cooperates and works harmoniously as they brainstorm on the components of Integrated Science. Link to other Learning Areas: The learner can link the importance of science to career pathways in Pre-technical Studies

substrands.name: Laboratory Safety
learning_outcomes: identify common hazards and their symbols in the laboratory
explain the causes of common accidents in the laboratory
describe First Aid measures for common laboratory accidents
appreciate the importance of safety in the laboratory and access to a healthy working environment.
learning_experiences: brainstorm on common hazards and their symbols
discuss causes of common laboratory accidents and their related First Aid measures
collaboratively role-play some First Aid procedures for common accidents in the laboratory
practise safety measures in the laboratory and the general school learning environment
discuss the importance of safety measures in the laboratory
use digital or print media to search for information on laboratory safety procedures.
inquiry_questions: 1. What causes accidents in the laboratory 2. What safety measures should be considered while working in the laboratory?
core_competencies: Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to Learn: the learner learns new concepts and identifies their talents as they role-play some First Aid procedures for common accidents in the laboratory.

Critical thinking and Problem-solving: the learner reflects and identifies solutions to some challenges that require First Aid while role-playing some First Aid procedures for common accidents in the laboratory. Values: Unity: the learner harmoniously works with peers as they role-play some First Aid procedures for common accidents in the laboratory. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs) Safety: the learner learns some safety measures to take as they practise safety measures in the laboratory and the general school learning environment. Link to other Learning Areas: The learner can relate safety and the importance of safety measures in the laboratory to safety measures at workplace in Pre-Technical studies.

substrands.name: Laboratory apparatus and instruments
learning_outcomes: describe the basic skills in science
use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory
use the SI units for basic and derived quantities in science
appreciate consumer protection when handling different apparatus, instruments, and other materials in day-to-day life.
learning_experiences: discuss the meaning and use of basic skills in science

practise use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory, (for heating, measuring mass, temperature, length, volume, weight, magnification, and time) (include parts, functions, and care of a light microscope; and parts of a bunsen burner)

collaboratively carry out activities on measurements of basic quantities and express them in the International System of Units (SI) (length, mass, time, electric current, temperature, amount of substance, light intensity)
work with peers to carry out activities to determine derived units from basic units (area, volume, speed, density)
• collect packaging with labels of quantities and discuss the importance of the information on labels.
inquiry_questions: 1. Why are basic science skills important?
2. How are quantities in science expressed?
core_competencies: Learning to Learn: the learner practises the use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory.
Communication and Collaboration: the learner collaboratively carries out activities on measurements of basic quantities and expresses them in the International System of Units.
values: Respect: the learner works harmoniously with peers when carrying out activities to determine derived units from basic units working.
Responsibility: the learner learns how to care for apparatus and instruments as they practise how to care for and use them in the laboratory.
pertinent_issues: Socio-economic issues: the learner links the quantity of goods parked to their prices as they collect packaging with labels of quantities and discuss the importance of the information on labels
links_to_other_areas: The learner can link the packaging of goods and labels of quantities from inputs and product labels learnt in Agriculture.
The learner uses mathematical manipulation skills in recording and carrying out measurements.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to separate homogeneous mixtures using appropriate methods.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: The learner consistently separates all the homogeneous mixtures using appropriate methods.
assessment_rubric.meets: The learner separates all of the homogeneous mixtures using appropriate methods.
assessment_rubric.approaches: The learner separates most of the homogeneous mixtures using appropriate methods.
assessment_rubric.below: The learner separates a few homogeneous mixtures using inappropriate methods.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to identify acids and bases using litmus paper.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: The learner correctly and exhaustively identifies any substances as acids or bases.
assessment_rubric.meets: The learner correctly identifies all of the provided substances as acids or bases.
assessment_rubric.approaches: The learner correctly identifies most of the provided substances as acids or bases.
assessment_rubric.below: The learner correctly identifies a few of the provided substances as acids or bases.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to outline applications of acids and bases in real life.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: The learner outlines all the applications of acids and bases exhaustively.
assessment_rubric.meets: The learner outlines the applications of acids and bases.
assessment_rubric.approaches: The learner outlines most of the applications of acids and bases.
assessment_rubric.below: The learner outlines a few applications of either acids or bases.

substrands.name: Mixtures
learning_outcomes: separate homogeneous mixtures using appropriate methods
outline applications of separating homogeneous mixtures in day-to-day life
appreciate the use of different methods of separating mixtures in day-to-day life.
learning_experiences: collaboratively categorise the mixtures as homogeneous or heterogeneous
discuss the meaning of the terms solvent, solute, and solution
share tasks as they carry out activities to separate homogeneous mixtures
discuss the applications of separating mixtures in day-to-day life
use digital or print media to search for more information on fraction distillation as a method of separating a mixture.
inquiry_questions: How is the separation of mixtures important in day-to-day life?
core_competencies: Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and Collaboration: the learner learns data presentation as they work collaboratively to categorise the mixtures as homogeneous or heterogeneous.

Learning to Learn: the learner learns how to separate various mixtures as they carry out activities to separate homogeneous mixtures. Values: Unity: the learner works harmoniously with peers while carrying out activities to separate homogeneous mixtures. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues: Peer Education and Mentorship: the leaner practises sharing of tasks as they carry out activities to separate homogeneous mixtures. Link to other Learning Areas: The learner can relate methods of separating mixtures in cereals to heterogeneous mixtures in Agriculture.

substrands.name: Acids, Bases and Indicators
learning_outcomes: identify acids and bases using a litmus paper
prepare an acid-base indicator from plant extracts
describe the physical properties of acids and bases
outline applications of acids, bases, and indicators in real life
appreciate the uses of acids and bases in r eal life.
learning_experiences: use litmus paper to classify household solutions into acids and bases
work with peers to prepare acid-base indicators from plant extracts, and dispose of laboratory waste responsibly.
use acid-base indicators from plant extracts to classify common household solutions as either acidic or basic
collaboratively carry out activities to investigate the physical properties of acids and bases
use digital or print media to explore applications of acids and bases.
inquiry_questions: Why are acids and bases important?
core_competencies: Core competencies to be developed:
Communication and Collaboration: the learner acquires data recording and presentation techniques as the learners carry out activities to investigate the physical properties of acids and bases.
Critical thinking and Problem-solving: the learner develops research skills as they explore applications of acids and bases using print or digital media.
Creativity and Imagination: the learner acquires innovative practises as they use acid-base indicators from plant extracts to classify common household solutions as either acidic or basic. Values:
Responsibility: the learner engages in assigned roles as they carry out activities to prepare acid-base indicators from plant extracts collaboratively.

Respect: the learner works with peers and recognises each other’s contribution(s) as they prepare acid-base indicators from plant extracts, and dispose of laboratory waste responsibly. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Environmental Education: the learner learns how to use flowers sparingly to protect plants as they use acid-base indicators from plant extracts to classify common household solutions as either acidic or basic. Link to other Learning Areas: The learner can relate the content of acids and bases to testing soil acidity and application of lime and fertilizers to improve soil fertility and pH in Agriculture.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to describe functions of parts of the male and female reproductive system.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: The learner describes all functions of parts of the male and female reproductive system comprehensively.
assessment_rubric.meets: The learner describes all functions of parts of the male and female reproductive system.
assessment_rubric.approaches: The learner describes most of the functions of parts of the male and female reproductive system.
assessment_rubric.below: The learner describes a few functions of parts of the male or female reproductive system.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to develop a plan to manage developmental challenges during adolescence.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: The learner fully develops an innovative plan to manage developmental challenges during adolescence systematically.
assessment_rubric.meets: The learner fully develops a plan to manage developmental challenges during adolescence.
assessment_rubric.approaches: The learner partially develops a simple plan to manage developmental challenges during adolescence.
assessment_rubric.below: The learner develops a sketchy plan to manage developmental challenges during adolescence partially

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to identify parts of the excretory system and their functions.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: The learner identifies all parts of the excretory system and their functions exhaustively.
assessment_rubric.meets: The learner identifies all parts of the excretory system and their functions satisfactorily.
assessment_rubric.approaches: The learner identifies most parts of the excretory system and their functions.
assessment_rubric.below: The learner identifies a few parts of the excretory system and their functions.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to develop and maintain a daily log of activities that promote skin and kidney health
assessment_rubric.exceeds: The learner comprehensively develops and maintains a purposeful daily log of activities that promote skin and kidney health.
assessment_rubric.meets: The learner satisfactorily develops and maintains a daily log of activities that promote skin and kidney health.
assessment_rubric.approaches: The learner partially develops and maintains a simple daily log of activities that promote skin and kidney health.
assessment_rubric.below: The learner partially develops and maintains a daily log of activities that promote skin or kidney health leaving out some key parts.

substrands.name: Human Reproductive System
learning_outcomes: identify parts of the male and female reproductive systems
describe functions of parts of the male and female reproductive system
describe the physical changes that take place in boys and girls during adolescence
develop a plan to manage developmental challenges during
appreciate that physical changes in boys and girls during adolescence have social and reproductive implications.
learning_experiences: Learners is guided to:
use charts and other print materials to observe and identify parts of the male and female reproductive systems
discuss the functions of parts of the male and female reproductive systems and share
use print and non-print material to search for information on physical changes that take place in boys and girls during adolescence
use print and non-print material to search for information on developmental challenges during adolescence
discuss with peers the coping mechanisms for developmental challenges during adolescence
Collaborate with peers and develop a plan to manage developmental challenges during adolescence.
inquiry_questions: 1. What are the physical, social, and emotional changes that take place during adolescence?
2. How are developmental changes managed during adolescence?
core_competencies: Self-efficacy: the learner develops confidence as they learn how to manage developmental challenges during adolescence.
Communication and Collaboration: the learner acquires speaking, listening skills, and self-expression as they discuss with peers the coping mechanisms for developmental challenges during adolescence.
values: Integrity: the learner shows self-discipline in coping with developmental challenges during adolescence.
Respect: the learner learns how to live harmoniously with peers already experiencing different developmental challenges as they develop a plan to manage developmental challenges during adolescence.
pertinent_issues: Human Sexuality: the learner develops the skill of self-awareness as they discuss with peers the coping mechanisms for developmental challenges during adolescence.
links_to_other_areas: The learner can relate content on the reproductive system in humans to reproductive systems in other animals in Agriculture.

substrands.name: Human Excretory System
learning_outcomes: identify functions of parts of the human skin
identify functions of parts of the urinary system in human
describe the causes of kidney disorders in human beings
develop and maintain a daily log of activities that promote skin and kidney health in human beings
appreciate the need for a healthy lifestyle to promote kidney and skin health.
learning_experiences: use a hand lens to observe the external parts of the skin (hair and sweat pores)
use a chart or model to discuss on parts and functions of the human skin
search for information on the waste products excreted through the skin (excess salts and water in sweat), lungs (carbon IV oxide), and kidneys (excess salts and water in urine)
discuss parts of the urinary system
use locally available materials to model the urinary system
use charts/ models/ animations to discuss the external parts and functions of the human kidney
use print and non-print materials to search for information on the causes and prevention of kidney disorders
search for information on healthy lifestyles that promote kidney and skin health
collaborate with peers to develop a daily log of activities that promote skin and kidney health.
inquiry_questions: 1. What is the role of the excretory system?
2. How can a healthy excretory system be maintained?
core_competencies: Communication and Collaboration: the learner acquires speaking and listening skills as they discuss parts of the urinary system.
Self-efficacy: the learner develops confidence as they search for information on healthy lifestyles that promote kidney and skin health.
values: Love: the learner appreciates and embraces their natural skin as they develop and maintain a daily log of activities that promote skin and kidney health.
Unity: the learner works collaboratively and harmoniously with peers as they develop a daily log of activities that promote skin and kidney health.
pertinent_issues: Health Promotion Issues: the learner learns how to improve skin and kidney health as they develop a daily log of activities that promote skin and kidney health.
links_to_other_areas: The learner can relate the content on healthy lifestyles that promote kidney and skin health linked to nutrition for healthy skin and kidneys in Agriculture.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to identify sources of electricity in the environment.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: The learner identifies all the sources of electricity in the environment exhaustively.
assessment_rubric.meets: The learner identifies all the common sources of electricity in the environment.
assessment_rubric.approaches: The learner identifies most of the sources of electricity in the environment.
assessment_rubric.below: The learner identifies a few sources of electricity in the environment.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to identify common electrical appliances used in day-to-day life.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: The learner exhaustively identifies common electrical appliances used in day-to-day life.
assessment_rubric.meets: The learner identifies all common electrical appliances used in day-to-day life.
assessment_rubric.approaches: The learner identifies most of the common electrical appliances used in day-to-day life.
assessment_rubric.below: The learner identifies a few common electrical appliances used in day-to-day life.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to identify safety measures observed when handling electrical appliances.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: The learner identifies all safety measures observed when handling electrical appliances correctly and exhaustively.
assessment_rubric.meets: The learner identifies all safety measures observed when handling electrical appliances correctly.
assessment_rubric.approaches: The learner identifies most of the safety measures observed when handling electrical appliances correctly.
assessment_rubric.below: The learner identifies a few safety measures observed when handling electrical appliances.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to identify the uses of magnets in day-to-day life.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: The learner correctly identifies all the uses of magnets in day-to-day life exhaustively.
assessment_rubric.meets: The learner identifies all uses of magnets in day-to-day life correctly.
assessment_rubric.approaches: The learner identifies most uses of magnets in day-to-day life correctly.
assessment_rubric.below: The learner identifies a few uses of magnets in day-to-day life correctly.

substrands.name: Electrical Energy
learning_outcomes: identify sources of electricity in the environment
connect simple electrical circuits to demonstrate the flow of electric current
identify common electrical appliances used in day-to-day life
identify safety measures observed when handling electrical appliances
appreciate the use of electricity in day-to-day life.
learning_experiences: discuss the sources of electricity in the environment

use print or digital media to search for more information on sources of electricity in nature (hydro-electric power, geothermal, solar, wind power, nuclear, tidal-wave, fossil fuels, biomass, natural gas, electrical cells)
collaboratively set up simple electrical circuits in series and in parallel (using electrical cells, connecting wires, switch, bulb, bulb holder) to demonstrate the flow of electric current
discuss common electrical appliances used in day-to-day life (pressure cooker, electric cooker, electric blender
electrical lamp and torch, electric iron box, electric kettle, electric guitar, electric fan, air conditioner, electric oven, television, electric speaker, washing machine and electric refrigerator.)
discuss safety measures observed when using electrical appliances
collaboratively explore uses of electricity in day-to-day life
use digital or print media to search for more information on electrical appliances and safety measures observed when using them.
inquiry_questions: 1. What are the sources of electricity in the environment?
2. How is electricity used in day-to-day life?
core_competencies: Learning to Learn: the learner learns how to set up a simple electric circuit as they carry out activities of series and parallel circuits.
Communication and Collaboration: the learner collaboratively works with peers to set up simple electrical circuits in series and parallel.
values: Unity: the learner with peers harmoniously set up simple electrical circuits in series and parallel.

Responsibility: the learner practises carefully handles various apparatus as they set up simple electrical circuits in series and parallel while working. Link to other Learning Areas: The learner can relate concepts in electrical circuits to electrical energy in Pre-Technical Studies

substrands.name: Magnetism
learning_outcomes: demonstrate the properties of a magnet
classify materials as magnetic or non-magnetic
identify the uses of magnets in day-to-day life
appreciate the applications of magnets in day-to-day life.
learning_experiences: collaboratively carry out activities to demonstrate properties of a magnet (attractive and repulsive, directional, poles and magnetic strength properties)
carry out activities to investigate the nature of force between different poles of magnets (basic law of magnetism)
use a permanent magnet to test different materials, sort and classify them into either magnetic or non-magnetic materials
discuss the applications of magnets in day-to-day life (separation of mixtures in radios, speakers, refrigerator doors, magnetic compass, and magnets used in toys to give magic effect)
• use digital or print media to search for information on applications of magnets in day-to-day life.
inquiry_questions: How are magnets used in day-to-day life?
core_competencies: Communication and Collaboration: the learner collaborates with others to carry out activities to demonstrate the properties of a magnet.
values: Responsibility: the learner diligently engages in assigned roles when carrying out activities to investigate the nature of force between different poles of magnets.
Unity: the learner works with others harmoniously to carry out activities to demonstrate the properties of a magnet.
pertinent_issues: Socio-economic Issue: the learner links different materials to their cost based on magnetic properties as they use a permanent magnet to test different materials, sort, and classify them into either magnetic or non-magnetic materials.
links_to_other_areas: The learner can link the concept learnt in magnetism to the application of magnets and magnetic materials in Pre-Technical studies.
